title: [Workshop] AI Engineering 101
talk_summary: A beginner workshop teaching AI engineering fundamentals by building a Telegram bot that calls OpenAI APIs: chat completions with a messages-array memory, tokenization/embeddings, a hand-rolled RAG pipeline over scraped MDN docs (chunking, cosine distance, context stuffing), few-shot code generation, image generation, and Whisper speech-to-text. It is introductory and mostly explains mechanics rather than reporting measured results.

takeaways.technique: Explicit chunk-size + overlap tuning for retrieval
takeaways.what_they_do: Chunks documents to a fixed token budget with a recursive splitter and adds overlap so semantic meaning isn't cut mid-sentence; they note chunk size is domain-specific (dense docs need smaller chunks than prose).
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you have overlap there you will have two separate chunks that have the same information in it
takeaways.numbers: chunk size ~1000 tokens, embedding model limit ~8000

takeaways.technique: Retrieve-then-stuff with explicit 'say I don't know' grounding
takeaways.what_they_do: Embed the question, rank stored chunks by cosine distance, take top-N up to a token budget, and put them in a prompt that forbids answering outside the context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if the question can't be answered based on the context say I don't know so we don't want it to speculate

takeaways.technique: Cheap deterministic settings for factual tasks
takeaways.what_they_do: Uses low temperature and top_p for documentation Q&A to reduce variance/hallucination, and tweaks only one sampling knob at a time.

takeaways.technique: Few-shot style anchoring for generated code
takeaways.what_they_do: Puts 1-2 input/output examples plus style rules (JSX, inline styles) in the system prompt so generated code matches house conventions without restating them each request.
takeaways.evidence_quote: here are two input output examples for code generation please follow these

takeaways.what_they_do: Describes tools to the model so it emits function name+args, letting one chat handler dispatch to image/code/math tools instead of hardcoded slash commands; also offloads math to a Python eval rather than trusting the LLM.

takeaways.technique: Run small open models locally on CPU
takeaways.what_they_do: Recommends whisper.cpp (C++ rewrite) and Stable Diffusion for local CPU inference instead of paid APIs when the model is small enough.
takeaways.evidence_quote: somebody took the whisper model and rewrote it in C++ so that it would run on CPU cores better
